added: registered qualifier semantics (stage L): a registered qualifier's meaning must be realised by an explicit clause-level construction, not inferred from lexical anchor overlap
change_scope.guarantee: A draft rejected by v1.1 is rejected by v1.2. The only new outcome v1.2 can produce is a rejection v1.1 did not.
change_scope.unchanged: every stage, code, threshold and policy inherited from v1 and v1.1, including stage E's half-anchor qualifier score, which still runs
change_scope.why_not_a_higher_anchor_threshold: Raising stage E's half-anchor rule to 75% or 100% is the same lexical heuristic with a different constant. It would reject faithful prose that renders a qualifier's meaning in other words - a false reject - and would still pass a verbatim canonical copy whose anchor overlap happens to be total, which is DF-01 itself at 5/6. The threshold is not the defect; measuring vocabulary in place of meaning is.

delegation_note: Stage F delegates to scripts/46 rather than re-encoding its rules. A second copy of the composition rules would be unversioned and could drift out of agreement with the one whose 71-case regression is the evidence that it works.

pipeline.checks: every declared claim is composition-safe and allowlisted
no proposition beyond what the declared claims license
every figure and unit traces to a declared claim
conditions and qualifiers survive; modality does not gain force
every visible material unit is written in the section language
registered semantic constraints: a claim's declared meaning survives and its declared forbidden meaning is not asserted
registered qualifier semantics: a registered qualifier's required meaning is realised by an explicit construction in the declared scope, and its denied generalised scope is not asserted
pipeline.code_policy: No new code. QUALIFIER_DROPPED for an absent required meaning; SEMANTIC_SCOPE_MISMATCH only where prose actively states the generalised scope the qualifier denies.
pipeline.scope: required meaning at paragraph scope, forbidden generalisation at unit scope - matching stage K, for the same reason: a qualifier lives outside the claim's own sentence, while an asserted meaning is made by one sentence
pipeline.unregistered_claims: a unit declaring no registered claim receives no failure from this stage

pipeline.checks: delegated to the frozen SEC-02-2 composition validator, at both unit and paragraph scope
every claim binds to its own registered source key
every material unit is claim-bound and cited
no internal identifier or pipeline vocabulary in visible prose

policy.auto_repair_rationale: A failed sentence must be visible as a failure. Asking the generator to fix it inside the same attempt launders an unsupported proposition into an apparently successful draft, and the audit trail then records a pass.
policy.no_lexical_proxy_rationale: Where a qualifier is registered, anchor overlap with the claim's own vocabulary does not discharge it. Stage E's score still runs and can still reject; it can no longer accept on its own.
policy.no_translation_repair_rationale: The validator rejects a mistranslated unit; it never translates one. Repairing input inside the validator would turn a translation failure into a pass and record it as one.
policy.pilot_policy_rationale: In v1 an optional rejected unit rejects the whole pilot rather than being dropped. Silently discarding failures would make the acceptance rate a function of how much prose was thrown away.

qualifier_semantics.generality: A claim acquires a rule by carrying a registered entry whose declared scope matches its allowlist row. No pilot sentence appears in the matching logic or in any entry.

properties: the named claim is allowlisted and declares the entry's required claim scope
the entry's qualifier_text equals the frozen allowlist qualifier byte for byte
the claim's own canonical sentence does not satisfy the entry's constructions
registry_integrity.rationale: A registry that has drifted from the frozen claims silently protects nothing, and an entry a verbatim canonical copy would satisfy cannot distinguish semantic realisation from reproduction - which is DF-01. Both are terminal, not warnings.
